name: Male infertility with azoospermia or oligozoospermia due to single gene mutation
aliases: Genetic male infertility with sperm production defects

ethnicAssociations: No specific ethnic predilection; reported worldwide

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic diagnosis of monogenic male infertility

criteria.description: Confirmed azoospermia or severe oligozoospermia on at least two semen analyses
Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic single gene mutation associated with spermatogenic failure
Exclusion of other acquired or multifactorial causes of male infertility such as obstruction, infection, or hormonal imbalance
Clinical history consistent with primary testicular failure without secondary causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of azoospermia or oligozoospermia plus identification of a pathogenic single gene mutation with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic counseling is recommended following molecular diagnosis.

laboratory: Semen analysis showing azoospermia or severe oligozoospermia
Elevated serum FSH with normal or low LH
Normal or low serum testosterone levels
imaging: Testicular ultrasound showing reduced testicular volume and heterogeneous echotexture
other: Histopathology of testicular biopsy showing spermatogenic arrest or Sertoli cell-only syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: Evidence of ductal obstruction on imaging or vasography

redFlags: Complete absence of sperm despite normal ejaculate volume
Elevated FSH indicating primary testicular failure
Family history of male infertility or consanguinity
references: O'Flynn O'Brien KL, et al. Genetic causes of male infertility. Nat Rev Urol. 2010.
Orphanet: Male infertility with azoospermia or oligozoospermia due to single gene mutation (ORPHA:399805)
Krausz C, Riera-Escamilla A. Genetics of male infertility. Nat Rev Urol. 2018.
